claim: The success rate in the discovery of novel, safe and effective pharmacotherapies has been declining steadily over the last few decades.
source: The success rate in the discovery of novel, safe and effective pharmacotherapies has been declining steadily over the last few decades (Scannell et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Scannell et al., 2012.

claim: Research rigor is estimated to be lacking in 50–90% of preclinical studies.
source: One area requiring immediate attention is research rigor, which is estimated to be lacking in 50–90% of preclinical studies (Freedman et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Freedman et al., 2015.

claim: High risk of failure is an inherent part of developing innovative therapies.
source: High risk of failure is an inherent part of developing innovative therapies (DiMasi et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to DiMasi et al., 2016.

claim: Some risks in developing innovative therapies can be greatly reduced and avoided by adherence to evidence-based rigorous research practices.
source: However, some risks can be greatly reduced and avoided by adherence to evidence-based rigorous research practices.
evidence: The claim is presented as a statement following discussion of risks in therapy development, with supporting context from multiple citations in the surrounding text.

claim: Numerous analyses have clearly identified measures that need to be taken to improve research rigor.
source: Indeed, numerous analyses conducted to date have clearly identified measures that need to be taken to improve research rigor (Begley and Ioannidis, 2015; Landis et al., 2012; Ritskes-Hoitinga and Wever, 2018; Vollert et al., 2020; Volsen and Masson, 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to published analyses.

claim: Improving research rigor has biomedical, societal, personal, economic and ethical benefits for academia and industry alike.
source: Improving research rigor has biomedical, societal, personal, economic and ethical benefits for academia and industry alike, since the development of novel therapies is often rooted in academic discoveries and requires a highly specialized effort of industry to translate these discoveries into clinically useful applications.
evidence: The claim is stated as a general assertion based on the relationship between academic and industry research.

claim: The EQIPD consortium was formed in 2017 with founding members from 29 institutions across eight different countries.
source: To address this challenge in preclinical biomedical research in a collaborative manner, the Enhancing Quality in Preclinical Data (EQIPD; originally called European Quality in Preclinical Data) consortium was formed in 2017 with founding members from 29 institutions across eight different countries (https://quality-preclinical-data.eu).
evidence: The claim provides factual information about the formation of the EQIPD consortium.

claim: The EQIPD consortium works closely with a large group of associated collaborators, advisors and stakeholders representing research institutions, publishers, funders, learned societies and professional societies, from more than 100 organizations in Europe and the US.
source: The consortium works closely with a large group of associated collaborators, advisors and stakeholders representing research institutions, publishers, funders, learned societies and professional societies, from more than 100 organizations in Europe and the US.
evidence: The claim provides factual information about the EQIPD consortium's collaborations.

claim: EQIPD defines research quality as the extent to which research data are fit for intended use.
source: EQIPD defines research quality as the extent to which research data are fit for intended use (for related definitions and explanations, see Juran and Godfrey, 1999; Gilis, 2020).
evidence: The claim is a definition provided by EQIPD with supporting citations.

claim: The EQIPD consortium has developed a quality system that is free for anyone to use.
source: The EQIPD consortium has developed a quality system that is free for anyone to use.
evidence: The claim is a direct statement about the EQIPD quality system.

claim: The development of the Good Laboratory Practice (GLP) standards was triggered by poor research practices that compromised human health.
source: For example, the development of the Good Laboratory Practice (GLP) standards, introduced first by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in the late 1970s, was triggered by poor research practices that compromised human health, such as mis-identification of control and experimental animals, omitted, non-reported or suppressed scientific findings, data inventions, replacements of animals lost to follow-up, and mis-dosing of animals (Bongiovanni et al., 2020; Marshall, 1983).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Bongiovanni et al., 2020 and Marshall, 1983.

claim: GLP standards were introduced first by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in the late 1970s.
source: For example, the development of the Good Laboratory Practice (GLP) standards, introduced first by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in the late 1970s, was triggered by poor research practices that compromised human health, such as mis-identification of control and experimental animals, omitted, non-reported or suppressed scientific findings, data inventions, replacements of animals lost to follow-up, and mis-dosing of animals (Bongiovanni et al., 2020; Marshall, 1983).
evidence: The claim provides historical information about GLP standards with supporting citations.

claim: GLP does not provide explicit guidance regarding aspects of study design, conduct, analysis and reporting that are important to minimize the risk of bias and make research robust.
source: However, GLP does not provide explicit guidance regarding those aspects of study design, conduct, analysis and reporting that are important to minimize the risk of bias and make research robust.
evidence: The claim is an assertion about the limitations of GLP based on the authors' analysis.

claim: The EQIPD Quality System is a novel system specifically aimed at supporting innovation in preclinical biomedical research.
source: In contrast, the EQIPD Quality System is a novel system specifically aimed at supporting innovation in preclinical biomedical research.
evidence: The claim is a direct statement about the EQIPD Quality System.

claim: The ultimate goal of the EQIPD Quality System is to improve the efficiency of developing novel effective and safe therapies.
source: While the direct consequence of installing a quality system will be the generation of research data that are of higher rigor, the ultimate goal is to improve the efficiency of developing novel effective and safe therapies.
evidence: The claim is a direct statement about the goal of the EQIPD Quality System.

claim: EQIPD was started in October 2017.
source: EQIPD was started in October 2017 and during the first phase (until June 2018), three work packages of the EQIPD consortium have delivered:
evidence: The claim provides factual information about when EQIPD started.

claim: A working group of 20 members from the EQIPD consortium nominated 75 statements that could define a functional quality system in non-regulated research.
source: During the second phase (July 2018 - January 2019), a working group was assembled from the EQIPD consortium members (n = 20). Based on the collected information, the working group nominated 75 statements that could define a functional quality system in non-regulated research.
evidence: The claim provides factual information about the development process.

claim: After three Delphi feedback rounds and two consensus meetings, the 75 statements were revised, resulting in a final list of 18 core requirements.
source: After three Delphi feedback rounds and two consensus meetings, these statements were revised, resulting in a final list of 18 core requirements (Table 2; see below for details).
evidence: The claim provides factual information about the development process.

claim: An updated version of the EQIPD framework was released for beta-testing in November 2019.
source: Based on the feedback from those pilot implementation sites and interactions with the stakeholder group, an updated version of the framework was released for beta-testing in November 2019.
evidence: The claim provides factual information about the release timeline.

claim: The final version of the EQIPD quality system was released in September 2020.
source: The final version of the quality system was released in September 2020.
evidence: The claim provides factual information about the release timeline.

claim: The EQIPD Quality System is meant to support scientists in triggering changes in research practices.
source: These principles delineate in a maximally concise and direct form that the EQIPD Quality System is meant to support scientists in triggering changes in research practices, and that it will help to identify objectives and direction of change but will not prescribe any specific solutions as long as the research processes are kept transparent and traceable.
evidence: The claim is a direct statement about the purpose of the EQIPD Quality System.

claim: The EQIPD Quality System will help to identify objectives and direction of change but will not prescribe any specific solutions as long as the research processes are kept transparent and traceable.
source: These principles delineate in a maximally concise and direct form that the EQIPD Quality System is meant to support scientists in triggering changes in research practices, and that it will help to identify objectives and direction of change but will not prescribe any specific solutions as long as the research processes are kept transparent and traceable.
evidence: The claim is a direct statement about the approach of the EQIPD Quality System.

claim: Research environments are highly diverse with different needs for researchers at big pharma companies, biotechs, CROs, and academic labs.
source: Research environments are highly diverse: the needs of researchers at a big pharma company are different from those at a biotech; the needs of CROs are different from those of academic labs, etc.
evidence: The claim is a statement based on general knowledge of research environments.

claim: Improving data quality is a challenge that cannot be tackled using a one-size-fits-all solution.
source: Thus, improving data quality is a challenge that cannot be tackled using a one-size-fits-all solution and flexibility is a critical requirement for future success.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the diversity of research environments.

claim: Flexibility is a critical requirement for future success in improving data quality.
source: Thus, improving data quality is a challenge that cannot be tackled using a one-size-fits-all solution and flexibility is a critical requirement for future success.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the diversity of research environments.

claim: EQIPD has reviewed research quality expectations of several major public funders and pharmaceutical companies.
source: For example, EQIPD has reviewed research quality expectations of several major public funders and pharmaceutical companies.
evidence: The claim provides factual information about EQIPD's activities.

claim: Summaries of research quality expectations and examples of how these expectations can be met are available for downloading from the EQIPD's online Toolbox.
source: Summaries of these expectations as well as examples of how these expectations can be met are available for downloading from the EQIPD's online Toolbox (https://eqipd-toolbox.paasp.net).
evidence: The claim provides factual information about available resources.

claim: The Process Owner should be someone who directs the work of the research unit and is knowledgeable about the importance of quality in research.
source: Typically, the Process Owner should be someone who directs the work of the research unit (e.g. group leader, principal investigator, CEO or department head) and is knowledgeable about the importance of quality in research.
evidence: The claim is a recommendation from EQIPD about the Process Owner role.

claim: EQIPD expects the Process Owner to be identified at the very first step of implementing the EQIPD Quality System.
source: EQIPD expects the Process Owner to be identified at the very first step of implementing the EQIPD Quality System (Table 2; core requirement #1).
evidence: The claim is a direct statement about EQIPD's expectations.

claim: The EQIPD Quality System does not replace and does not intend to re-interpret any of the existing rules, policies and other quality systems that apply to the research unit's environment.
source: The Process Owner may also be asked and should be prepared to explain that the EQIPD Quality System does not replace and does not intend to re-interpret any of the existing rules, policies and other quality systems (which focus on specific areas) that apply to the research unit's environment.
evidence: The claim is a direct statement about the relationship between EQIPD and existing systems.

claim: EQIPD does not want to be associated with organizations that engage in or tolerate unacceptable ethical practices or legal violations.
source: First, EQIPD does not want to be associated with organizations that engage in or tolerate unacceptable ethical practices or legal violations.
evidence: The claim is a direct statement about EQIPD's position.

claim: The EQIPD Quality System is focused on quality, not legislation.
source: Second, the EQIPD Quality System is focused on quality, not legislation.
evidence: The claim is a direct statement about the focus of the EQIPD Quality System.

claim: It is not acceptable to waste animals due to poor study design, conduct or analysis.
source: Clearly, it is not acceptable to waste animals due to poor study design, conduct or analysis.
evidence: The claim is a statement based on ethical considerations.

claim: Ethical concerns on the use of animals in research have promoted the creation of a legal framework in almost every country.
source: Ethical concerns on the use of animals in research have promoted the creation of a legal framework in almost every country (e.g. Animal Welfare Act in the US; Directive 2010/63 in the EU).
evidence: The claim is supported by examples of legal frameworks.

claim: Scientific evidence demonstrates that many aspects of animal care and use that are beyond the legal requirements have a direct impact on research results.
source: Scientific evidence demonstrates that many aspects of animal care and use that are beyond the legal requirements have a direct impact on research results (Guillén and Steckler, 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Guillén and Steckler, 2020.

claim: Implementation of the EQIPD Quality System does not require researchers to stop or reduce ongoing experimental work.
source: Implementation of the EQIPD Quality System does not require researchers to stop or reduce ongoing experimental work.
evidence: The claim is a direct statement about the implementation process.

claim: The EQIPD Quality System is designed so that it takes only minimal effort to sign up and begin the journey toward a quality system.
source: It is designed so that it takes only minimal effort to sign up and begin the journey toward a quality system that should help researchers gradually improve certain quality aspects of their work.
evidence: The claim is a direct statement about the design of the EQIPD Quality System.

claim: EQIPD recommends that scientists apply protection against risks of bias for every study and unambiguously disclose the protective measures used.
source: In general, EQIPD recommends that scientists apply protection against risks of bias for every study and unambiguously disclose the protective measures used.
evidence: The claim is a direct statement of EQIPD's recommendation.

claim: Each study has a particular purpose and the rigor applied to the study should be defined, documented in advance and be commensurate with the purpose of the study.
source: Each study has a particular purpose and the rigor applied to the study should be defined, documented in advance and be commensurate with the purpose of the study.
evidence: The claim is a direct statement of EQIPD's recommendation.

claim: There are modes of research that can tolerate a certain level of uncertainty and do not lead to a formal knowledge claim.
source: There are modes of research that can tolerate a certain level of uncertainty and do not lead to a formal knowledge claim (see Appendix 1 Glossary for definition).
evidence: The claim is a statement based on understanding of different research modes.

claim: For research that is conducted with the prior intention of informing a knowledge claim, EQIPD requires that maximal possible rigor is applied.
source: For research that is conducted with the prior intention of informing a knowledge claim, EQIPD requires that maximal possible rigor is applied (and exceptions explained and documented in the study plan; see Table 4).
evidence: The claim is a direct statement of EQIPD's requirement.

claim: EQIPD requires that investigators assert in advance whether a study will be conducted to inform a formal knowledge claim.
source: EQIPD requires that investigators assert in advance whether a study will be conducted to inform a formal knowledge claim (core requirement #10; Table 2), and that they explicitly state this in the study (experimental) plans prepared before studies and experiments are conducted.
evidence: The claim is a direct statement of EQIPD's requirement.

claim: The ultimate mission of the EQIPD Quality System is to serve the entire community of scientists conducting non-regulated preclinical biomedical research.
source: The ultimate mission of the EQIPD Quality System is to serve the entire community of scientists conducting non-regulated preclinical biomedical research.
evidence: The claim is a direct statement about the mission of the EQIPD Quality System.

claim: Early adopters are of critical value in every field where a cultural change is under discussion.
source: Such early adopters are known to be of critical value in every field where a cultural change is under discussion.
evidence: The claim is a statement based on general knowledge about change management.

claim: Academic initiatives have successfully addressed research data management and sharing of best practices by introducing Data Champions that serve as local advocates for good data practices.
source: For instance, academic initiatives have successfully addressed research data management and sharing of best practices by introducing Data Champions that serve as local advocates for good data practices (e.g. https://www.data.cam.ac.uk/intro-data-champions).
evidence: The claim is supported by a reference to an example.

claim: The early adopters of the EQIPD Quality System will help optimize the balance between the benefits of implementing such a system and any potential adverse consequences through their feedback to the EQIPD consortium.
source: The early adopters of the EQIPD Quality System, through their feedback to the EQIPD consortium, will help optimize the balance between the benefits of implementing such a system and any potential adverse consequences (e.g. resources allocated, reduction in conventional indices of scientific productivity).
evidence: The claim is a statement about the expected role of early adopters.

claim: Not all research units are equally prepared or willing to implement a Quality System.
source: It is a general understanding that not all research units are equally prepared or willing to implement a Quality System, an effort that requires investing time and resources.
evidence: The claim is a statement based on general understanding.

claim: The EQIPD Quality System can be implemented at any level (university, research institute, company, or a laboratory).
source: The EQIPD Quality System can be implemented at any level (university, research institute, company, or a laboratory).
evidence: The claim is a direct statement about the applicability of the EQIPD Quality System.

claim: EQIPD encourages the transition toward better quality practices at the level of individual labs, departments or research groups, no matter how small they are, provided that there is a researcher capable, authorized and willing to take on the role of Process Owner.
source: While this is the desired case, EQIPD encourages the transition toward better quality practices at the level of individual labs, departments or research groups, no matter how small they are, provided that there is a researcher capable, authorized and willing to take on the role of Process Owner.
evidence: The claim is a direct statement of EQIPD's position.

claim: The EQIPD Quality System is not intended to be used at the level of individual projects.
source: The EQIPD Quality System is not intended to be used at the level of individual projects.
evidence: The claim is a direct statement about the intended use of the EQIPD Quality System.

claim: Using the EQIPD Quality System at the level of individual projects may create confusion and increase the risk of errors as the same people within a research unit may follow separate research quality practices depending on the project that they are working on.
source: Otherwise, it may create confusion and increase the risk of errors as the same people within a research unit may follow separate research quality practices depending on the project that they are working on.
evidence: The claim is an inference about potential negative consequences.

claim: The Process Owner is expected to use a self-assessment form provided by EQIPD to check whether Core Requirements and research unit-specific needs are appropriately addressed.
source: The Process Owner is expected to use a self-assessment form provided by EQIPD to check whether Core Requirements and research unit-specific needs are appropriately addressed.
evidence: The claim is a direct statement about EQIPD's expectations.

claim: The self-assessment allows the Process Owner to monitor performance of the quality system.
source: The self-assessment serves two purposes. On the one hand, it allows the Process Owner to monitor performance of the quality system.
evidence: The claim is a direct statement about the purpose of self-assessment.

claim: The self-assessment provides the base for an external assessment.
source: On the other hand, it provides the base for an external assessment.
evidence: The claim is a direct statement about the purpose of self-assessment.

claim: External assessment of the research unit, performed as peer review, is a quality verification step that is recommended and important for the full implementation and the successful maintenance of QS.
source: The external assessment of the research unit, performed as peer review, is a quality verification step that is recommended and important for the full implementation and the successful maintainance of QS.
evidence: The claim is a direct statement about the importance of external assessment.

claim: External assessment is not required and adopters of the Quality System may stop at the self-assessment stage.
source: However, this step is not required and adopters of the Quality System may stop at the self-assessment stage.
evidence: The claim is a direct statement about the requirements for external assessment.

claim: Research units that successfully implemented the EQIPD Quality System receive a certificate of EQIPD compliance.
source: Research units that successfully implemented the EQIPD Quality System receive a certificate of EQIPD compliance.
evidence: The claim is a direct statement about the outcome of successful implementation.

claim: Several research units have completed the implementation of the EQIPD Quality System and have been evaluated by the EQIPD team.
source: Several research units have completed the implementation of the EQIPD Quality System and have been evaluated by the EQIPD team.
evidence: The claim provides factual information about implementation progress.

claim: External assessment is currently performed by scientists that developed the EQIPD Quality System.
source: External assessment is currently performed by scientists that developed the EQIPD Quality System.
evidence: The claim provides factual information about current assessment practices.

claim: A training module for future assessors will be released to ensure the reliability and consistency of assessments conducted by different experts.
source: A training module for future assessors will be released to ensure the reliability and consistency of assessments conducted by different experts.
evidence: The claim is a statement about future plans.

claim: The EQIPD team evaluates and compares the reliability of hybrid external assessment models combining onsite visits and remote interviews.
source: Moreover, anticipating a large demand for external assessments, the EQIPD team evaluates and compares the reliability of hybrid external assessment models combining onsite visits and remote interviews.
evidence: The claim provides factual information about ongoing evaluation activities.

claim: On September 30, 2020, the EQIPD Quality System was released for broad deployment and unrestricted use by the research community.
source: On September 30, 2020, the EQIPD Quality System was released for broad deployment and unrestricted use by the research community.
evidence: The claim provides factual information about the release date.

claim: The EQIPD team is implementing a governance model to enable the maintenance and further development of the EQIPD framework beyond the IMI project phase.
source: To enable the maintenance and further development of the EQIPD framework beyond the IMI project phase, the EQIPD team is implementing a governance model (Figure 3).
evidence: The claim provides factual information about future plans.

claim: The EQIPD team is actively engaged in discussions with funders (public and private) and publishers to develop instruments and mechanisms that will allow scientists to further benefit from the use of the EQIPD Quality System.
source: The EQIPD team is actively engaged in discussions with funders (public and private) and publishers to develop instruments and mechanisms that will allow scientists to further benefit from the use of the EQIPD Quality System.
evidence: The claim provides factual information about ongoing activities.

claim: The EQIPD Quality System has 18 core requirements organized into six categories: Research team, Quality culture, Data integrity, Research processes, Continuous improvement, and Sustainability.
source: Table 2. EQIPD Core Requirements.
evidence: The claim is evident from Table 2 which lists all 18 core requirements organized by category.

claim: The EQIPD Quality System was supported through the European Union's Innovative Medicines Initiative.
source: Supported through the European Union's Innovative Medicines Initiative (IMI), the EQIPD consortium, among other deliverables, aimed to develop a novel preclinical research quality system that can be applied in both the public and private sectors.
evidence: The claim provides factual information about funding support.

claim: The EQIPD Quality System was designed to be suited to boost innovation by ensuring the generation of robust and reliable preclinical data while being lean, effective and not becoming a burden that could negatively impact the freedom to explore scientific questions.
source: Such a quality system should be suited to boost innovation by ensuring the generation of robust and reliable preclinical data while being lean, effective and not becoming a burden that could negatively impact the freedom to explore scientific questions.
evidence: The claim is a direct statement about the design goals of the EQIPD Quality System.

claim: Fitness of research data is defined by the stakeholders, who can be scientists themselves, but also patients, funders, sponsors, publishers, and collaboration partners.
source: Fitness, in this context, is defined by the stakeholders, who can be scientists themselves, but also patients, funders, sponsors, publishers, and collaboration partners (e.g. peers in a multi-site research project).
evidence: The claim is a direct statement about who defines fitness in the EQIPD context.

claim: EQIPD is preparing training, support and assessment services for those research units that successfully implement the quality system and would like to seek formal accreditation.
source: Further, EQIPD is preparing training, support and assessment services for those research units that successfully implement the quality system and would like to seek formal accreditation.
evidence: The claim provides factual information about EQIPD's planned services.

claim: The essence of the EQIPD Quality System is the set of 18 core requirements that can be addressed flexibly, according to user-specific needs and following a user-defined trajectory.
source: The essence of the EQIPD Quality System is the set of 18 core requirements that can be addressed flexibly, according to user-specific needs and following a user-defined trajectory.
evidence: The claim is a direct statement from the abstract about the essence of the EQIPD Quality System.

claim: A sustainable EQIPD Quality System will ultimately serve the entire community of scientists conducting non-regulated preclinical research, by helping them generate reliable data that are fit for their intended use.
source: Building upon the feedback from users and continuous improvement, a sustainable EQIPD Quality System will ultimately serve the entire community of scientists conducting non-regulated preclinical research, by helping them generate reliable data that are fit for their intended use.
evidence: The claim is a direct statement from the abstract about the ultimate goal of the EQIPD Quality System.
